papers.title: Exploiting Adiabatic Softening for Defect-Free Hot Forging of Ti-6Al-4V Femoral Stems
papers.abstract: Hot forging of Ti-6Al-4V is extensively utilized in the manufacture of orthopedic implants; however, the coupled influence of strain rate and temperature on ductile damage evolution during the forging of femoral stems remains insufficiently quantified. In this study, a finite element framework is developed to analyze and optimize the hot forging process, incorporating strain rate- and temperature-dependent plasticity, as well as the Johnson–Cook damage criterion. Mesh convergence is established, and the assumption of quasi-adiabatic conditions is substantiated via Péclet number analysis. A full factorial design is implemented by varying the ram velocity (0.1–0.5 m/s) and initial billet temperature (850–950 °C) to evaluate the forging load, stress triaxiality, equivalent plastic strain, and damage accumulation. Results indicate that process kinetics govern the mechanical response: increasing the ram velocity enhances strain-rate hardening, resulting in higher peak loads, while explicitly reducing stress triaxiality and suppressing ductile damage evolution. Conversely, temperature exhibits a secondary influence within the investigated domain. Validation of the damage criterion confirms safe operating windows, identifying low-velocity forging as a high-risk condition for localized defect formation. These findings provide practical guidelines for the strain-rate-based optimization of thermomechanical processing parameters for Ti-6Al-4V femoral stems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V热锻造，而非增材制造，因此与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper concerns conventional hot forging of Ti-6Al-4V femoral stems, not additive manufacturing (LPBF/SLM/EBM/DED) of Ti-6Al-4V, so it does not meet the directional requirement for L1.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究热锻过程中应变率和温度对Ti-6Al-4V股骨柄延性损伤的影响。
summary_zh.method: 建立有限元框架，结合Johnson-Cook损伤准则，全因子分析不同工艺参数。
summary_zh.result: 高冲压速度抑制损伤，低速度导致局部缺陷。
summary_zh.validation: 通过损伤准则验证确定安全工艺窗口。

summary_en.motivation: To quantify the coupled influence of strain rate and temperature on ductile damage evolution during hot forging of Ti-6Al-4V femoral stems.
summary_en.method: A finite element framework incorporating strain rate- and temperature-dependent plasticity and the Johnson-Cook damage criterion was developed and analyzed via full factorial design.
summary_en.result: Increasing ram velocity enhances strain-rate hardening and reduces damage, while temperature has a secondary effect.
summary_en.validation: Damage criterion validation confirmed safe operating windows.
